reading.body:
This campus publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, the largest published figure in Iowa, though only 2 of 52 mapped data center facilities in the state have disclosed their power footprint. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 9 MW of IT load suggests roughly 225 racks, a scale suitable for distributed workloads or smaller training clusters rather than the largest model runs.

The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, and TIA-942, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and government. Its 420,000 square feet of technical space indicates a large physical plant, but published specifications do not disclose total campus power draw, PUE, cooling technology, or grid interconnection details needed to assess its actual constraint on deployment.

Iowa's total published data center IT capacity stands at 18 MW across two disclosed facilities. This campus represents over half of that small total, making the state negligible in the context of national AI infrastructure. The state context provides no information on power availability, transmission capacity, or whether this facility faces grid constraints that would limit further expansion, facts material to whether it matters for scaling AI compute.
